newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canwest told Australia it would sell - Asper.
newsitem.headline: Canwest told Australia it would sell - Asper.

text.p: The Australian government had been told in February this year that Canwest Global Communications Corp was willing to reduce its stake in the unlisted television station operator Network Ten, Canwest chairman Izzy Asper told a court on Thursday.
Asper said he told Treasurer Peter Costello at a meeting on February 11 that an orderly float of stakes held by Canwest and two other companies, Selli Pty Ltd and Donholken Pty Ltd, was possible.

He also told the Federal Court that there had been constant attempts over the past four years to take Ten back into the public arena but all the shareholders could not agree on how this could be achieved.
Canwest and the two companies began the court action in an attempt to overturn a government ruling on May 2 that they divest their shares in Ten.

They are also seeking to overturn a ruling by the Australian Broadcasting Authority (ABA) one month earlier that Canwest had unlawful control of Ten, even though the Canadian company had a voting stake of only 14.99 percent.
Canwest has an economic interest of 76 percent in Ten and has been ordered to lower this to at least 57.5 percent, a level which has previously been sanctioned by the ABA.

Canwest financed the acquisition by Selli of the shareholding in Ten from advertising industry leader John Singleton. It also financed Donholken's purchase of the Ten stake held by minority investors Robert Whyte and Jack Cowin.
Asper told the court that neither he nor Canwest exercised control over Selli or Donholken.
